content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: hold the current plan (P0). Payments and general are both predicted at 100% service level for 15:30-17:30, against an 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"Payments calls have run above forecast since 13:45, reaching 103 vs 70.5 (+46%) at 15:15, when service level dropped to 23.3%. All call reasons rose together, and no marketing send or incident explains it. Staffing is at plan (31 of 31 agents), so the cause is extra calls, not missing staff. Even so, the forecast for the disruption window (15:30-17:30) is 100% service level on both queues with 0% abandons if nothing changes. The rest-of-day figure is 98.6%. No policy issues.","trade_offs":["P2 (lend 3 general agents to payments plus IVR callback, 15:30-16:30) is also free and predicts the same 100%, with rest of day slightly better at 98.8%. However, it moves people off general for no predicted gain in the window.","P3 (cancel payments coaching and delay breaks) costs INR 750 and gives no improvement in the window. Rest of day is 98.5%, and it disrupts agents' coaching and break time.","P4 (chat deflection of 10% of payment status enquiries) costs INR 96 for the same 100% in the window, with rest of day at 98.4%."],"watch":"The latest actual service level was 23.3%, while the prediction is 100%, and the cause of the surge is unknown. Check payments volume and service level at each interval. If calls keep climbing or service level stays low, switch to P2: it is free, can be in place quickly, and predicts no harm to general."}
